fields.Intro Paragraph 1: What reckons the "Acceptable Year of the Lord?" In this 13th episode of Inner Whirled, Dylan and I are again joined by Crrow777, as we go beyond the obvious zodiacal significance of the 12 apostles and consider the Old Testament patriarchs of Israel's dozen tribes. We also look at the fascinating solar footage Crrow and others have filmed of a strange second sun. Members will enjoy a solid three and a half hour examination as we continue to honor the work of the renegade Reverend Robert Taylor.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: They cover the acceptable year of Our Lord as a solar cycle rather than a historical ministry, the sky as the missing Q source that resolves the synoptic problem, Plutarch's first-century proof linking Helios to Kyrus, Israel as a Phoenician word for Kronos, the full zodiacal mapping of the 12 Tribes and their Patriarchs, Miriam decoded as Venus through the "leprous as snow" passage, and how the Vatican's Renaissance bounty system seeded the historical canon with deliberate forgeries.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Precession, the Calendar and the Sky Clock", "body": "Crow presses a question he admits he cannot answer: the old symbolism puts Cancer at the height of the sun's power around June 21, yet precession has shifted the sky since those allegories were written. Dylan answers that precession is real, since almanacs and ephemerides keep being updated, that the tropical cycle was built to account for it, and that the Gregorian is the most precise calendar we have had. Crow grants its accuracy but calls it a mechanism of control, insisting the only real measure of time is the sky clock, that solar noon is when the sun stands highest, and that separation from nature is separation from truth."}, {"title": "Why Dylan Would Throw It All Out", "body": "Dylan lays out a view he has rarely shared: his language work convinces him these texts are products of the Middle Ages, so the allegories cannot be trusted to preserve an ancient sky, and the most useful move is to throw it all out. He traces this to approaching scripture as a committed Christian who wants plain answers rather than secret keys, warning that a civilization hoarding knowledge risks starting over. Crow agrees the maps we grew up with are forgeries but mourns what could be lost, and Dylan adds that mystery schools rewrite the system whenever they take power, so none of it should be taught as history."}, {"title": "Twelve Patriarchs, Twelve Signs", "body": "The members' hour turns to Taylor's central claim that the patriarchs number exactly twelve because the zodiac does, and that the word tribe names the path the sun travels through the signs. Genesis 37:9, where the sun, moon and eleven stars bow down, frames the twelfth star, and the apparent thirteenth tribe created by adopting Ephraim and Manasseh is resolved by moving Levi into the priesthood. Taylor then names Reuben, Ephraim, Judah and Dan as the four royal tribes, the genii of winter, spring, summer and autumn, whose man, bull, lion and eagle still accompany the four evangelists and reappear on the tarot's Wheel of Fortune."}, {"title": "Decoding the Signs One Tribe at a Time", "body": "Working sign by sign, Dylan argues the swords of Simeon and Levi were more likely a trident or harpoon suited to the fishes of Pisces, and that Simeon sits remarkably close to the Greek word for a sign. Chance notices that the King James unicorn of Deuteronomy 33:17 lands beside Taurus, where the constellation Monoceros first appears in the early seventeenth century, the same century as that translation. Dylan openly rejects Taylor's fish tail case for Capricorn as unsatisfying, then offers his own reading of Benjamin's ravening wolf as Lupus between Libra and Scorpio, a hunter of dusk and dawn standing for balance."}, {"title": "Emotion, Hypocrisy and Being Wrong in Public", "body": "After honoring Taylor while conceding his flaws, the hosts turn to how truth gets delivered. Dylan says heated emotion buys attention and virality but leaves no room to retreat when you turn out to be wrong, and that he recently re-edited his earlier books to strip much of that charge out. Chance adds that passion literally means suffering and that negative emotion is rooted in denial, whether of oneself or felt from outside. Dylan closes that what truly inflames people is hypocrisy: if you use inflammatory language you had better be right, because being loudly wrong hands critics the material to use against you later."}]
